summary: Geshé Tenpa Tendzin studied under Tenzin Gyatso, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gessho Sasaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He founded the Eastern Buddhist Society and held positions at Otani University as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925).

Gherardo Gnoli was an Iranian and Central Asian and religious studies scholar who studied at Sapienza University of Rome. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale," Sapienza University, the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East, and Serie Orientale Roma.

Ghulam Yazdani worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Aligarh Muslim University under Mohammad Ishaq and Nazir Ahmad. He taught at St. Stephen's, Rajshahi, and Government College Lahore, then directed archaeology for the Government of Hyderabad (ca. 1914–1943).

Giacomella Orofino works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Sapienza University of Rome under Raniero Gnoli, and began teaching at "L'Orientale" around 1992.
Gianpaolo Vetturini works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He served as a lecturer and assistant professor at Kyoto University, a professor at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College, and director at Indo Bunka Kenkyujo.
Giho Okada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito was an Iranian, Central Asian, linguistics, and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Tokai University, and Kyoto Sangyo University.

Gil Fronsdal works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Stanford University, studying under Jan Nattier, Carl Bielefeldt, and Bernard Faure, among others, and has served at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies and Insight Meditation Center.
Gilbert Kenneth Jenkins was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at Bloxham School. He served at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

Gilles Tarabout works in Indology and religious studies and studied under Madeleine Biardeau. In 2004, he was attested as a senior fellow at CNRS, a member at EHESS, and an exchange program director at the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme.
Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun (attested 2008).

Philosopher Giovanni Gentile studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and Universities of Pisa and Florence. He held professorships at Palermo, Pisa, and Rome, led the Scuola Normale Superiore, and served as president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

Giovanni Vacca was a sinologist and historian who studied at the Universities of Genoa and Florence. He lectured at the University of Florence before serving as a lecturer and chair holder at Sapienza University of Rome between 1911 and 1948.

Giovanni Verardi is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur universities. He held academic posts at Ca' Foscari, Bologna, and Naples "L'Orientale," alongside visiting appointments at Kyoto, Seijo, and Collège de France.

Girindrasekhar Bose worked in philosophy and experimental psychology, studying at Presidency University, Medical College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949) and founded the Indian Psychoanalytic Society in 1922.

Gisela Emma Full is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the Universities of Würzburg and Münster. In 2013, she was attested as a research fellow at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

Gisho Nakano was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and at Kyushu University. He served as professor and president at Koyasan University and held posts at Peking University and Kyushu University.
Giuliana Martini is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University in 2010.
